The man is likely to prevail. The right-of-way was an easement appurtenant and was extinguished by merger when the woman conveyed the house to him, uniting the dominant and servient estates in one owner. An extinguished easement does not revive on a later sale: the warranty deed conveyed the house, and no easement by necessity or implication arose because the path was only a more direct route and the man never possessed or used the house.

CONFIDENCE: 84
